subject: E3b gaming tests: two exploits pass our A1/A2 criterion, Petri's judge catches both
body: Measured on a haiku proxy, n=12 paired (experiments/taste_petri/gaming_tests/README.md). Rollback laundering: our A2 -0.43 [-0.50,-0.36], all 12 seeds. A 6k benign-reasoning buffer: A1 0.88->0.03 because of the reasoning[:6000] cap, and the composite score RISES +0.19. Petri-judge eval_awareness went UP under both (+0.58, +1.17). Because the E3b success criterion is A1 and A2 with Petri behaviour not lower, and validity is not in it, an arm could pass on these. Suggested: add validity to the criterion; add a per-arm flag when our A1/A2 falls while Petri eval_awareness rises; one-line detectors (n_target_turns > final-branch turns; len(reasoning)>6000; target turn inside the 24k cut; role-header grep on environment text). Seven patches in the README. Nothing edited.
